Project overview

  • Client / Context: Independent Commission (Mobile Configurator & E-Commerce Integration)
  • Core skills demonstrated: Mobile UX architecture, end-to-end product design, competitor benchmarking, technical requirement definition, design systems, visual identity, conversion rate optimisation (CRO).

What this project proves about me: I can take technically dense, high-cognitive-load configuration journeys and translate them into clean, conversion-focused mobile experiences backed by systematic design thinking.

The challenge

Building a custom PC is an intimidating process fraught with cognitive friction. Builders must cross-reference multi-layered hardware compatibility—such as motherboard chipsets, CPU socket architectures, GPU dimensions, and power supply unit (PSU) wattage—while continually balancing a strict personal budget across multiple merchant inventories.

In 2019, the market presented two extremes: established desktop tools like PCPartPicker, which were technically exhaustive but visually overwhelming and poorly optimised for handheld mobile devices, or simplistic buying guides that lacked customisation and direct purchasing paths. Mobile users faced clunky, unresponsive tables, disjointed navigation, and dead-end configuration workflows.

The challenge was to engineer an intuitive, mobile-first iOS/Android utility that gave novice builders clarity and expert enthusiasts granular spec filtering, while bridging the drop-off gap between planning a rig and executing the purchase.

My process

To ensure both commercial viability and ergonomic mobile utility, I structured the engagement across five iterative phases:

  1. Discovery & Strategic Research: Competitor audits, market gap analysis, and user persona mapping.
  2. Product Requirements & System Architecture: Defining core feature hierarchies, data models, and API integration paths.
  3. Brand Identity & Visual Foundations: Establishing brand psychology, accessible palette systems, and iconography.
  4. Low-Fidelity Prototyping & Flow Mapping: Rapid pen-and-paper ideation followed by structured greyscale wireframes.
  5. High-Fidelity UI, Accessibility Pivot & Design System: Iterating from an aesthetic dark UI to a readable light design system, concluding in component specification.

What I did

1. Discovery, User Segmentation, and Gap Analysis

I initiated discovery by auditing existing desktop configurators and emerging mobile apps. The research exposed a critical drop-off point: users frequently drafted builds on their smartphones but abandoned the journey when trying to locate compatible parts across fragmented retailers.

I visualised user needs across distinct cohorts—ranging from budget-constrained students and first-time builders needing guardrails, to gaming enthusiasts and business professionals requiring uncompromising spec validation.

Early concept slide defining the core value proposition: bridging hardware selection, budget limits, and direct e-commerce checkout.

Target audience analysis segmenting user expectations across gamers, students, and workstation developers.

Strategic alignment documentation establishing core UX and business benchmarks prior to wireframing.

2. Information Architecture and Functional Requirements

Synthesising research insights and technical feasibility requirements, I established the minimum viable product (MVP) scope around five architectural pillars:

  • Persistent Multi-Build Management: Allowing users to draft, name, and compare parallel builds (e.g., 'Streaming Rig' vs. 'Office Workstation').
  • Real-Time Financial Transparency: Dynamic live-updating sub-totals and grand totals pinned to the interface to eliminate checkout sticker shock.
  • Deep-Dive Hardware Cards: Progressive disclosure patterns allowing users to browse high-level specs and tap through for deep socket/clock-speed validation.
  • Amazon API Bridge: A contextual conversion path transforming passive spec lists into an active multi-item Amazon cart.

3. Visual Identity and Accessibility Foundations

Before committing to interaction design, I developed the brand identity. Modern consumer hardware tools often default to aggressive, hyper-stylised gamer branding that alienates non-technical users. I opted for a clean, precision-driven visual language, testing 2019's subtle elevated planar style to achieve tactile mobile depth.

Systematic logo explorations testing icon marks, circular frame geometries, and contrast across varied digital surfaces.

I paired a primary Prussian Blue with vivid Cerulean accents to balance professional authority with crisp interactive affordances.

The foundational application palette, establishing hex values across brand primaries, dark anchors, and accessible neutral surfaces.

4. Low-Fidelity Exploration and Wireframing

To solve ergonomic challenges on mobile devices, I drafted rapid paper wireframes focusing on thumb-zone accessibility for high-frequency actions—such as swapping components and filtering specifications. I subsequently translated these sketches into digital wireframes to test navigation flows and screen-to-screen transitions.

Early thumb-zone sketches exploring part-drawer mechanics, persistent footer summaries, and listing patterns.

Low-fidelity wireframe sequence detailing the core configuration flow from dashboard to individual part search.

5. High-Fidelity UI and The Critical Design Pivot

I initially produced an extensive dark-theme UI, aligning with prevailing gaming aesthetics and 2019 OS dark-mode trends.

The initial dark-theme exploratory flow across cataloguing, hardware specification, and cart views.

However, usability evaluation and stakeholder review revealed a significant flaw: dense technical lists displaying serial numbers, megahertz ratings, and dimensions in low-contrast dark layouts induced high visual fatigue. The cognitive load was too heavy for rapid comparison.

I led an evidence-based pivot to a clean, high-contrast light design system. I engineered reusable UI cards, standard input fields, and modular navigation bars that heightened legibility and established trust.

The refined light-theme design system and screen flow, delivering crisp scannability and modular UI assets.

Why I made these decisions

  1. Pivoted from Dark UI to Light UI: While dark interfaces are popular within gaming cultures, they reduce legibility when scanning dense technical data, numerical lists, and small typography. Shifting to an airy, high-contrast neutral interface directly reduced cognitive load and improved scan speed.
  2. Adopted Progressive Disclosure for Hardware Specs: Showing complete motherboard compatibility sheets upfront would overwhelm novice builders. I designed a card system displaying key metrics (price, model, core clock speed) with tap-to-expand deep views, keeping the primary configuration screen manageable.
  3. Placed Sticky Financial Summaries Above the Fold: In custom PC builds, budget overruns are the primary cause of cart abandonment. Keeping cumulative spend visible eliminated apprehension and reinforced user confidence as parts were added.
  4. Designed Contextual Amazon Affiliate CTAs: Instead of forcing users out of the application to search third-party SKUs manually, I placed direct 'Buy from Amazon' and 'Add to Basket' buttons inline with each component, closing the gap between research and procurement.

Images in context

The final product transformed an overwhelming technical chore into a frictionless, guided mobile experience. Component cards feature unambiguous imagery, key metrics, and direct commerce integration.

In-situ validation testing: confirming one-handed reachability, card readability, and primary button tap targets within a natural holding grip.

Final high-fidelity screen displaying a complete 'Streaming Build', highlighting real-time cost calculation and Amazon affiliate conversion hooks.

Impact / results

Area Deliverable / Outcome
End-to-End Delivery Full lifecycle ownership from discovery and paper sketching to complete visual identity and production-ready high-fidelity UI specifications.
Design Architecture Developed a reusable, modular component library that enabled rapid layout of new hardware categories and streamlined future engineering handoff.
Commercial Alignment Converted a passive reference utility into an active conversion mechanism by designing an inline Amazon API procurement journey.
Heuristic Optimisation Successfully challenged initial client aesthetic assumptions (dark mode), defending and executing a high-contrast pivot that demonstrably enhanced readability and reduced data friction.

Tools and skills applied

Category Tools / skills
Design & Prototyping Adobe XD, Paper & Pen Wireframing, Rapid Sketching, Interactive Prototyping
Research & Strategy Competitor Benchmarking, User Persona Mapping, Feature Prioritisation, Gap Analysis
Design Systems & UI Modular Component Libraries, Mobile Layout Grids, Typography Scales, Colour Theory
Commercial & Tech Conversion Rate Optimisation (CRO), Amazon Affiliate API Mapping, Information Architecture (IA)

Roles performed on this project

  • Lead Product Designer: Defined end-to-end user journeys, wireframes, and design system components.
  • UX Researcher & Strategist: Executed competitive analysis, mapped user personas, and scoped core product requirements.
  • Brand Identity Designer: Developed the visual identity, iconography, and cohesive design system palette.

childMarkdownRemark.html: Building a custom PC involves navigating dense technical specifications, complex component compatibility, and volatile pricing across fragmented marketplaces. Commissioned to solve this high-friction journey on mobile, I led the end-to-end design of the PC Builder application from discovery through to high-fidelity interface specification. Conducting competitor benchmarking and audience segmentation, I translated complex system logic into an accessible configurator featuring real-time budget tallies, modular component drawers, and an Amazon API checkout bridge. After evaluating an initial dark-mode prototype against readability heuristics, I spearheaded an evidence-led pivot to a high-contrast light UI design system. The final deliverable provided a scalable, conversion-oriented mobile tool that transformed speculative parts lists into ready-to-order hardware baskets.
